To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mass dependence of the peak Ec.m. is linear, whereas the peak IMFs shows a power law dependence with tau \approx1.0.
The multiplicity of IMF increases with the increase in system mass.
the multiplicity, mass and energy of IMFs increase with the increase in system mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of mass dependence of IMFs in the central reactions of symmetric and asymmetric systems for different energies, different equations of state and different widths of gaussians.
the study of the emission of IMFs in the reactions of heavy ions at different energies.
the influence of system mass on emission of intermediate mass fragment in central collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power law dependence of peak IMFs with system mass is a universal feature for all the systems and for all the equations of state, cross-sections and Gaussian widths.
, the emission of IMFs is strongly mass dependent.
the system mass dependence of peak IMFs is not a unique function but depends on the various parameters used in the model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mass dependence of IMFs is similar to that of the light fragments and the mass dependence of IMF emission is independent of the type of the reaction, system masses, beam energies and different widths of Gaussian.
, the power law dependence of peak IMFs with system mass is a general feature for all the reactions and it is independent of the equation of state, nn-crossection and width of Gaussian.
the mass dependence of IMFs is similar to that of fragments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mass dependence of IMFs and fragments is independent of the equation of state and the method used to simulate the reaction.
, for a given energy in the c.m. frame and for a fixed width of the gaussian, there is a definite mass range for a given E/A in which the peak IMFs are produced.
the mass of the system has a profound influence on the emission of fragments and the emission is more for lighter systems.
